Class 4 · Chapter 8 of 9

Read scaled charts and compare results

Use axes, half-symbol keys and totals across displays.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Bills, budgets and rupees with paise. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can use a non-unit chart scale.
  • I can read half a pictograph symbol.
  • I can compare and update survey data.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Read the key first

This key says each ● is 2 children.

Count the symbols, then multiply by 2.

Three symbols mean 6 children.

Screen 2 of 4

Half a symbol is half the value

If a star is worth 10 stickers, half a star is worth 5.

Add the whole stars and the half star.

Two and a half stars is 25 stickers.

Screen 3 of 4

Compare the bars

Find the tallest and shortest bars.

Subtract to find how many more.

Read the scale on the side before you subtract.

Screen 4 of 4

Update the data

If 6 samples move from Lyra to Aster, take 6 off Lyra and add 6 to Aster.

The total stays the same.

Check that the two changes match.

Words to know
scale
How much one step or one symbol on a chart stands for.
pictograph
A chart that uses symbols to show counts.
key
The note that tells you what each symbol is worth.
survey
Asking a group the same question and recording the answers.

For parents

What your child learns

In a survey, the total is split between groups. When one group is not given, subtract the others from the total. Score tables let you add and then compare totals.

A common slip

Children may forget to find the missing group first. Subtract the known groups from the total. Then compare.

5-minute home activity: Survey the rest

  1. Ask 10 people which sport they like and tally the answers.
  2. Hide one group and work it out from the total.
  3. Say which group has the most and how many more.
  4. Write the result as a table.
